A <button> is a filled common button. An <a class="button"> is the same thing for a link. Put an <i> and wrap the label in a <span> — there is no icon-left / icon-right class. Add circle for a 40dp icon button.

Tokens follow the M3 button spec. Default height is 40dp, label is label-large, corners are 20dp (a stadium), icons are 18dp with an 8dp gap, and the horizontal inset is 24dp (16dp next to an icon). State layers are 8% hover and 10% focus or press. Disabled is on-surface at 38% on a 12% container.

{% call code() %} Link {% endcall %} {% endcall %} {% call section("filled", "Filled") %}

High emphasis. This is the default — the main action on a page. Container primary, label on-primary, no elevation. filled on a .btn is still accepted and does nothing extra.

Medium emphasis. Add tonal. Container secondary-container, label on-secondary-container.

{% call code() %} {% endcall %} {% endcall %} {% call section("outlined", "Outlined") %}

Medium emphasis, no fill. Add outlined (or border). Outline is outline, label is primary.

{% call code() %} {% endcall %} {% endcall %} {% call section("elevated", "Elevated") %}

Medium emphasis with a shadow. Container surface, label primary, elevation 1 at rest and 2 on hover. Use sparingly so the page does not fill with shadows.

{% call code() %} {% endcall %} {% endcall %} {% call section("text", "Text") %}

Low emphasis. Add text. No container, label primary. Use these inside cards and dialogs so they do not stack shadows.

{% call code() %} {% endcall %} {% endcall %} {% call section("icon", "Icon buttons") %}

Add circle for a 40dp icon button. The variant helpers still apply: default is filled, text is the standard (transparent) icon button, tonal and outlined match the common-button colors.

{% call code() %} {% endcall %} {% endcall %} {% call section("floating", "Floating") %}

A FAB is circle extra or circle large: 56dp, 16dp corners, primary-container, elevation 3. extra circle small is the 40dp small FAB. extend is the extended FAB — icon plus label at 56dp.
